high_alert_reason: ISMP high-alert: insulin. #1 medication-error cause of severe hypoglycemia in inpatient settings. Requires independent two-nurse verification for IV push or infusion initiation.
adult_dose: DKA: IV bolus 0.1 unit/kg then infusion 0.1 unit/kg/hr, titrate to glucose drop 50–75 mg/dL/hr. Hyperkalemia: 10 units IV + 25 g dextrose. Sliding scale: institution-specific.
pediatric_dose: DKA: avoid bolus; start 0.05–0.1 unit/kg/hr infusion.
renal_adjustment: Reduce dose in renal impairment; insulin clearance decreases with eGFR < 50.
max_dose: Infusion rate rarely exceeds 0.2 unit/kg/hr in DKA; persistent elevation prompts reevaluation, not dose escalation.
key_monitoring: Point-of-care glucose q1h during infusion, q30min during rapid correction
Volume and anion gap during DKA
Hypoglycemia signs — diaphoresis, altered mentation, tachycardia

provenance.source: ADA Standards of Care + ISMP high-alert list + Lexicomp summary
provenance.note: Five-rights workflow must enforce two-nurse check on initiation and concentration verification on every hang.
